why: rclcpp's type-erased base constructor; see the pubsub stage's `cpp:Publisher::PublisherBase`. RULED 2026-09-08 (phase-430 W7), and the ruling separates the HIERARCHY from the NAME. The hierarchy is DELETED: phase-417 W1.a had added `class TimerBase` with a virtual destructor and `detail::WallTimer` under it, RFC-0089 had already refused exactly that, and the argument is the executor's dispatch -- the callback slot is `nros_cpp_timer_callback_t`, a raw `void(*)(void*)`, dispatch goes through the STATIC `detail::WallTimer::trampoline`, so no virtual call through a `TimerBase*` existed or can; even the destructor's virtuality was dead, since the cell is built with `make_shared` and the control block already records the concrete deleter. `detail::WallTimer` now derives from nothing and `create_wall_timer` returns `std::shared_ptr<nros::Timer>` aliased onto the private cell. The NAME is KEPT, as a plain (NOT deprecated) alias for `rclcpp::Timer`, and that is measured rather than argued: deleting it turned `just colcon-parity` red, because that gate builds `examples/templates/local-msg-package` against a REAL /opt/ros install where `rclcpp::Timer` does not exist ('Timer' in namespace 'rclcpp' does not name a type; did you mean 'Time'?). With `cpp-port-minimal-publisher` vendored UNMODIFIED for the same reason, the alias is what keeps the intersection of "compiles under real ROS 2" and "compiles under nano-ros" non-empty for any ported node holding a timer. `WallTimer` and `GenericTimer` stay absent -- the clock axis is a runtime field plus the second verb `rclcpp::create_timer(node, clock, period, cb)`, not a type parameter -- and `timer_base_is_a_name_not_a_hierarchy.cpp` pins all of it: `is_same<TimerBase, Timer>`, `!is_polymorphic`, both nested `SharedPtr` spellings, and a self-tested detector for the continued absence of `WallTimer`.
